questions.problem: The lamina $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le x,\,0\le x\le 1\}$ has the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=3xy.$ Find the moment of the lamina about the $x$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{x}={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is represented as a type I plane region and $\lambda (x,y)=3xy.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}y\cdot 3xy\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}3x{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}3x{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot {[{y}^{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot {x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{5}{x}^{5}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: The lamina $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 1\}$ has the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{15{x}^{2}}{y}.$ Find the moment of the lamina about the $x$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{x}={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is represented as a type I plane region and $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{15{x}^{2}}{y}.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}y\cdot \frac{15{x}^{2}}{y}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}15{x}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}15{x}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}15{x}^{2}[{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}\,\text{d}y]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}15{x}^{2}\cdot [y]_{y={x}^{2}}^{y=1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}15{x}^{2}\cdot (1-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}15{x}^{2}-15{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[5{x}^{3}-3{x}^{5}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{x}={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is represented as a type I plane region and $\lambda (x,y)=3y\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}y\cdot 3y\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}3{y}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}3{y}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x[{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}3{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot {[{y}^{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{sin}^{3}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{{sin}^{4}⁡x}{4}]}_{x=0}^{x=\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: The lamina $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,\frac{1}{2}\le x\le 1,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡x\le y\le 0\}$ has the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=2{e}^{y}.$ Find the moment of the lamina about the $y$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{y}={∬}_{D}x\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is represented as a type I plane region and $\lambda (x,y)=2{e}^{y}.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}x\cdot 2{e}^{y}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2x{e}^{y}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}^{0}2x{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}2x[{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}^{0}{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}2x\cdot [{e}^{y}]_{y=\operatorname{ln}⁡x}^{y=0}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}2x(1-x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}2x-2{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[{x}^{2}-\frac{2{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{x=1/2}^{x=1} \\  & =(1-\frac{2}{3})-(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{12}) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: The lamina $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,{y}^{2}\le x\le 1,\,\frac{1}{2}\le y\le 1\}$ has the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{1}{x}.$ Find the moment of the lamina about the $y$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{y}={∬}_{D}x\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is represented as a type II plane region and $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{1}{x}.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}x\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}1\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}{\int }_{{y}^{2}}^{1}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}[x]_{x={y}^{2}}^{x=1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}1-{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[y-\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{y=1/2}^{y=1} \\  & =(1-\frac{1}{3})-(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{24}) \\  & =\frac{5}{24}.\end{aligned}
$$
